extracted.intended_audience: researchers preparing and submitting manuscripts to Royal Society journals (authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on preparing, formatting, and submitting manuscripts to Royal Society journals, including ethical, data, figure, and peer-review requirements. Covers initial submission, final files, and post-acceptance processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: When deciding on authorship and other contributors please consider equity, diversity and inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list of authors should meet the criteria provided on our authorship policy page. All contributors who do not meet all of these criteria should be included in the acknowledgements section.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID for submitting author
rubrics_metrics.description: The submitting author will be required to provide an Open Researcher and Contributor ID (ORCID) via the online submission system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision of ORCIDs by co-authors is strongly encouraged, but not mandatory. The benefits of registering an ORCID are outlined on the linked page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal-specific length and article-type rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that length restrictions (if any), article types and other journal specific information are available on the 'Author information' page on each journal website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should check the target journal's Author information page for specific limits and requirements before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism and image integrity screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are routinely screened for plagiarism and, where relevant, image integrity (e.g. paper-mills).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure originality and proper image handling; editors may request original data if concerns arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI and AI-assisted technologies policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Please refer to our policy on the use of Artificial intelligence (AI) and AI-assisted technologies in preparing your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are required to declare whether they have used AI technologies and provide a statement about how they were used; the statement will be published in the final article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: You are encouraged to suggest suitably qualified reviewers, especially from underrepresented groups (including women, ethnic minority scientists, scientists with disabilities and other underrepresented groups), early career researchers, and researchers from the global South.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may choose to use other reviewers; suggestions should be suitably qualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licence to publish requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors are required to grant us a licence to publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should read the licence to publish carefully before submission; open access papers are published under Creative Commons licences (details on the open access page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Royal Society journals only accept submissions in English. Spelling should be British English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviations should be used only when necessary and should be defined when they are first used. SI units should be used throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language editing services
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who believe their manuscripts would benefit from professional editing prior to submission are encouraged to use a language editing service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Royal Society has negotiated discounts with AJE and Charlesworth; Royal Society Open Science partnered with PaperPal Preflight; AuthorAid hosts resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format-free initial submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Format-free initial submission for the majority of journals: at first submission authors can submit their manuscript in any format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: Proceedings B and Biology Letters require a Word version upon initial submission to enable accurate length estimation. Authors are encouraged to consider readability for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editable final files and figure/table source files
rubrics_metrics.description: Once accepted the main manuscript must be submitted as an editable file, not a PDF, and the source files of any figures and tables must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting LaTeX, follow LaTeX guidelines; at final revision you will be required to provide source files (see LaTeX section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Your article title should be a short description of the research you are reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best titles are written with both human readers and search engines in mind; include keywords in your title to help discovery. Excessively long titles should be avoided. Title page should contain full names and affiliations for each author, except for journals operating double anonymous peer review (e.g. Proceedings B, Notes & Records).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should be no more than 200 words and should not contain references or unexplained abbreviations or acronyms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract should be concise, informative, readable as a standalone piece, summarise scope, main results and conclusions, and include likely search terms. Consider using IMRAD structure. The abstract provided at initial submission is included in reviewer invitation emails, so describe work clearly for potential reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Please include at least 3 and up to 10 keywords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overly broad or specialised terms; think of words you would use to search for articles on the same topic. Keywords can be short phrases and may include synonyms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main text structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The main text of your article should be split into clearly-labelled sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually background, methods, results, discussion and conclusions, but authors may use headings that best suit the article. Abbreviations should be written out in full on first use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods section completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Methods section should contain all elements necessary to allow interpretation and replication of the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full specific details of materials used (reagents, animal models, software). References to published methods or protocols may be provided (e.g. protocols.io). Preregistration of methods at a suitable repository is encouraged. Provide Data Availability statement and accession details where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field station and laboratory acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where authors have conducted research at or with the support of Field Stations and Marine Laboratories (FSMLs) etc, authors are encouraged to provide the names and locations of FSMLs in methods and acknowledgements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal recognition helps funders and managers track outputs and supports broader impact and accessibility goals. An example sentence is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgements
rubrics_metrics.description: Please acknowledge anyone who contributed to the study but did not meet the authorship criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledgements are the appropriate place for contributors not qualifying for authorship; CRediT roles should be used to specify contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding statement format
rubrics_metrics.description: Please state the sources of funding including grant number for each author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including this information is a requirement of many funders. Example format provided: 'This work was supported by the Wellcome Trust [grant numbers xxxx, yyyy]; the Natural Environment Research Council [grant number zzzz]; and the Economic and Social Research Council [grant number aaaa].' You will also enter funding details during submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: References style and dataset citations
rubrics_metrics.description: All journals use a system based on Vancouver style referencing. References are numbered in order of appearance at end of article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to datasets must be included in the reference list with DOIs where available; each reference should contain as many elements as possible (authors, year, title, journal, volume, pages, DOI). EndNote style files available for most journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Please submit a PDF as your main document. At final revision you will also be required to provide the source files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TeX files should preferably be generated using specified pdfTeX versions (TeX Live 2024/2025). All files required to compile TeX source must be uploaded (.tex, .bib/.bbl, .bst if specified). Do not send master TeX files containing file call-ups (except to figures and references); TeX file must be complete with all article sections. Figures must be supplied in accepted formats; Type 3 fonts not accepted; use vector fonts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and code availability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a requirement that data and code underlying a study are made publicly available, usually within a designated repository or from the supplementary material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must complete the data accessibility section in the submission form and list repositories, accession numbers, and other relevant details. It is not permitted to state that data will be available from the authors upon request. Cite datasets and code in the reference section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material can be used for supporting datasets, movies, figures and tables, and any other supporting material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger datasets should be uploaded to an appropriate repository rather than provided as supplementary material. The main article should stand on its own. References in supplementary material should be kept to an absolute minimum. Supplementary files are created by authors and are not edited by the Royal Society — proof-read thoroughly. Files up to 350MB accepted; very large files (e.g. movies) contact editorial office. All supplementary material will be published under CC-BY and posted on figshare (DOI). Ensure titles/descriptions provided during submission are accurate and informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and tables numbering and captions
rubrics_metrics.description: All figures and tables should be numbered and cited in the text. Figure and table captions are required and should be brief and informative and include any relevant copyright information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At initial submission, figures can be provided within the manuscript or as separate files. Images should be minimally processed and accurately reflect the original data. Authors should retain unprocessed data and metadata files, as editors may request them to aid evaluation. Final submission: figures should be uploaded as separate files and tables provided in an editable format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted figure formats and fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted figure formats: PNG, EPS, TIFF, JPG, JPEG. TeX/LaTeX-coded figures should be converted to PS or EPS. Type 3 fonts are not accepted; vector fonts preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines for document and image conversions in ScholarOne Manuscripts are available in the Get Help Now section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure label and numeric style
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested style for figure labels: Font: Times New Roman; 9pt, 11pt leading preferred; text should be no smaller than 7.5pt. Use a thin space between values and units (e.g. 300 nm). Thousands separated by thin spaces, not commas (e.g. 10 000 000). Insert a full space either side of equal-to sign (e.g. x = 300).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multipart figures: label parts alphabetically and consistently (left to right, then top to bottom); all figure parts labelled in the same position; if a label interferes place outside the figure part (top left). Alphabetical labels italicized in roman brackets, e.g. '(a)'. Sub-parts labelled using bracketed roman numerals, e.g. '(ii)'. Figure labels on coloured backgrounds should be placed inside a white circle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colour reproduction policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All figures will be published in colour online, but reproduced in black and white in any print versions by default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If print colour is essential, list the relevant figure numbers on submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure permissions for third-party material
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures from other sources should be fully acknowledged in the caption, and written permission sought for both print and electronic reproduction before being used (where relevant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For open access papers, CC-BY licence will cover all components; permission must be obtained to use third-party material under CC-BY and copyright holders must be aware of terms. If material cannot be included under CC-BY it must be identified in the text or to production team for appropriate copyright lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: End section statements at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the submission process you will be required to provide statements on Ethics, Use of AI, Data/code/materials, and Competing interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statements are essential for rapid assessment and will be automatically added to the paper if accepted. You are no longer required to add these statements in the manuscript itself — have them ready when submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics statement details
rubrics_metrics.description: Research on humans or human tissues requires a statement detailing ethical approval (name of body and project/licence number). For animal studies include ethical approval details and licence/approval number. Fieldwork approvals and specimen extraction approvals should be listed. Museum/fossil specimen details (specimen numbers and institutions) must be provided either in manuscript or supplementary files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ethics and policies page for more information on preparing this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors will be asked to declare whether they have used AI technologies in the preparation of their paper and to provide a statement about how they have used this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement will be published in the final article; read the AI policy for full details of allowed use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a statement if you have any competing interests to declare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competing interests are defined as those that could undermine the objectivity, integrity or perceived value of publication. See the Competing Interests section of the authorship policy for more information; contact editorial office if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRediT contributor roles
rubrics_metrics.description: The submitting author will be required to allocate roles to authors from the CRediT taxonomy (14 roles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This taxonomy is used to create an Authors’ Contributions section listing specific contributions for each author (roles include Conceptualization; Data curation; Formal analysis; etc.). More information at credit.niso.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers are normally peer reviewed in a single-anonymized fashion (author names not concealed, referee names are).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referee reports and other correspondence must remain confidential and should not be shared or made publicly available unless the journal is operating under open/Transparent peer review. Open peer review is optional for Proceedings A and mandatory for Proceedings B, Open Biology, Royal Society Open Science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access and licensing details
rubrics_metrics.description: Royal Society Open Science and Open Biology are fully open access journals; other journals are open access in 2026 through Subscribe to Open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open access papers are published under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC-BY) licence. CC-BY allows copying, distribution, transmission and adaptation provided attribution is given and not implying endorsement. Users do not need to notify authors or publisher when using material under CC-BY.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article transfer policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfers may be offered when an article does not meet the scope requirement of the original journal. Editors' comments and reviewer reports on the article are transferred and will be available to the receiving journal's editorial team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transferring is usually quicker than resubmitting; transferring is a two-step process and should be completed as soon as possible after receiving the offer — the offer expires after four weeks. A list of possible transfer destinations is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media summary for lay audience
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting final files you will be prompted to submit a media summary of no more than 100 words aimed at a lay audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline your research and relevant findings, highlight why the research is important, link research with examples or analogies, avoid excessive jargon or statistics. Ensure user details (institution, email, telephone) are up to date for press contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover image submission
rubrics_metrics.description: You are welcome to submit a potential cover image for use on the journal website and press site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you obtain all relevant copyright permissions before submitting. Upload as 'Cover Image' when submitting revised files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofing process and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The corresponding author will be sent a link to review the article proof through the Kriyadocs platform. All changes and queries are tracked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs should be read carefully and accuracy of tables, references and mathematical expressions checked. Major alterations to content should not be made at this stage. Only a few days may be available for checking proofs — inform the journal or make alternative arrangements if absent. Production queries to proofs@royalsociety.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offprint and reprint conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: On publication, authors will receive a link providing free access to the paper. Electronic reprints may NOT be used for commercial purposes or posted on openly accessible websites, unless published under a CC-BY licence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Printed issue copies can be purchased on request; contact sales team for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion and media embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to share and promote their work on social media and professional networks to maximise impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Society's press office promotes articles via weekly lists of media summaries to journalists. The Society employs a strict embargo policy — if approached by a journalist prior to publication contact the press office. Alert your institution's press office in advance so they may prepare a press release.
